<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915437_theRebbe_101" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915437_theRebbe_101__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section contains the opening header and date of the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Night of the 14th of Kislev, 5739*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section introduces the Zohar's explanation of the seven blessings, focusing on the seventh blessing which includes ten expressions of joy corresponding to the ten utterances.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">“Who created joy and gladness, groom and bride, exultation, song, delight, and cheer, love and brotherhood, peace and friendship.”</t>
    <t s="1">And the Rebbe, my father-in-law, brings in his maamar beginning with the words “This”</t>
    <t s="2">(in the pamphlet of wedding discourses of 5689)</t>
    <t s="3">the passage of the Zohar in Parshat Terumah</t>
    <t s="4">which explains there all seven blessings in detail,</t>
    <t s="5">and he says there regarding the seventh blessing</t>
    <t s="6">[which includes all the blessings],</t>
    <t s="7">“The seventh one sustains everything,</t>
    <t s="8">and from this seventh one all are blessed, certainly the inclusive principle of the ten utterances,</t>
    <t s="9">because this includes supernal and lower, and therefore it includes ten kinds of joy, etc.”</t>
    <t s="10">And he explains in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="11">that the inclusive principle of the ten utterances includes the Ten Commandments</t>
    <t s="12">(supernal)</t>
    <t s="13">and the Ten Utterances</t>
    <t s="14">(lower),</t>
    <t s="15">and since this blessing is the inclusive principle of the ten utterances, therefore it has ten expressions of joy</t>
    <t s="16">(aside from the words “groom and bride”)</t>
    <t s="17">which are the aspect of joy in each particular Sefirah</t>
    <t s="18">[for specifically through this the Sefiros are in their completeness,</t>
    <t s="19">as understood from what is explained in many places</t>
    <t s="20">on the verse</t>
    <t s="21">“The mother of the children is joyous”].</t>
    <t s="22">And the Zohar continues there</t>
    <t s="23">(brought in the maamar there)</t>
    <t s="24">regarding the seventh blessing,</t>
    <t s="25">“Fortunate are Israel, who merited below corresponding to the supernal pattern.”</t>
    <t s="26">And this is</t>
    <t s="27">that this blessing is</t>
    <t s="28">(also)</t>
    <t s="29">praise and thanksgiving to the Holy One, blessed be He, for that Israel, through their service, refine and purify the lower realm</t>
    <t s="30">(below)</t>
    <t s="31">so that it will be corresponding to the supernal pattern,</t>
    <t s="32">and through this they draw down the revelation of the Ein Sof, blessed be He, even into the supernal worlds</t>
    <t s="33">(above).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the concept of "merited below corresponding to the supernal pattern" in relation to groom and bride, and the ongoing revelation of the Giving of the Torah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And the explanation of the matter</t>
    <t s="2">(and also the connection of the matter of “merited below corresponding to the supernal pattern” to the matter of groom and bride),</t>
    <t s="3">is,</t>
    <t s="4">that all matters below are derived from their counterpart above,</t>
    <t s="5">and in the language of the Tanya</t>
    <t s="6">“that they were derived from them,”</t>
    <t s="7">and so it is with groom and bride</t>
    <t s="8">(below),</t>
    <t s="9">that they are derived from the groom and bride above,</t>
    <t s="10">the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Congregation of Israel.</t>
    <t s="11">And as explained in the Midrashim of our Sages, that the groom and bride mentioned in Song of Songs refer to the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Congregation of Israel.</t>
    <t s="12">And as our Sages, of blessed memory, said</t>
    <t s="13">“on the day of his wedding”</t>
    <t s="14">— this is the Giving of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="15">for the Giving of the Torah is the aspect of the marriage of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Congregation of Israel.</t>
    <t s="16">And it can be said that this is the aspect of “and a good heart makes a constant feast,”</t>
    <t s="17">for every single day there is the matter of the Giving of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="18">as we say in the blessing over the Torah</t>
    <t s="19">(which we bless every day)</t>
    <t s="20">“the Giver of the Torah” in the present tense,</t>
    <t s="21">to the extent that every day, whoever reads and reviews, the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him,</t>
    <t s="22">and the Alter Rebbe explains</t>
    <t s="23">that this that the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him is exactly like it was at the time of the Giving of the Torah the first time.</t>
    <t s="24">Therefore they said</t>
    <t s="25">(regarding practical law)</t>
    <t s="26">“Just as there [it was] with awe, fear, trembling, and perspiration, so too here [it must be] with awe, fear, trembling, and perspiration.”</t>
    <t s="27">And particularly according to what is explained</t>
    <t s="28">that these four expressions</t>
    <t s="29">(awe, fear, trembling, and perspiration)</t>
    <t s="30">correspond to the four letters of the Name Havayah,</t>
    <t s="31">for at the Giving of the Torah there was the revelation of the Name Havayah to each and every Jew,</t>
    <t s="32">and this revelation is also present in the engagement with Torah now.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
